newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro bourses roar ahead on stronger dollar.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro bourses roar ahead on stronger dollar.

text.p: European bourses roared ahead on Tuesday, with Paris and Frankfurt hitting new peaks, lifted by a strong rally on Wall Street and a stronger dollar, which held out prospects of cheaper exports from Europe.

The U.S. currency itself took a slight breather at the European close after hitting a 40-month high against the mark. The dollar has been driven by U.S. data showing buoyant economic growth and a belief the European single currency would turn out to be soft.
The startling rebound in European stocks was driven by domestic factors as well as the dollar and Wall Street, which was up nearly one one percent by the European close.

The biggest leap came in Paris, where shares climbed 3.0 percent to to finish up 85.78 points at 2,944.04 on the CAC-40 blue chip index, eclipsing the previous intra-day high of 2,903.18 set last Friday.
"It has been storming ahead," said one trader. "There has been quite a bit of activity... People are going into CAC-40 futures and a lot are going into the CAC-40."
The rebound from Monday's 1.1 percent loss was spurred by the robust dollar and technical factors linked to the expiry of share options contract on Monday, traders said.
Investors were also on the lookout for buying opportunities after Monday's losses.
"Fund managers are taking new positions. It's the reverse of yesterday," said one trader.

London shook off recent pre-budget gloom and soared by 2.7 percent to close at 4728.3 points, up 123.7, its biggest one-day points jump in nearly five years amid renewed bid speculation and buying interest in the futures market.
Talk of a bid for NatWest Bank played a part, dragging the banking sector sharply higher. NatWest shares ended up 40p to 847p, after hitting 858p.
"The futures took the market to these dizzying heights without a doubt," said one senior trader. "And the bank sector is very much involved, particularly NatWest."

Some analysts said the new Labour government's first budget on Wednesday was expected to contain harsh measures, which might avert the need to increase interest rates -- giving some comfort to the market.

In Frankfurt, floor trade ended with profits of nearly one percent on the DAX index and the IBIS index in electronic trade was up 1.8 percent near the close as the stronger dollar helped to lift the market from Monday's losses.
The 30-share DAX index close at 3,819.85 points, up 34.08, surpassing the record closing high set last Thursday at 3,805 points.
The export-dependent chemical sector stole the spotlight, boosted by the dollar and prospects of bigger profits from exports.

Carmakers also benefited from the stronger dollar as luxury carmaker Porsche AG surged 210 marks to 2,530 marks after Lehman Brothers raised its price target for Porsche to 3,600 marks from 3,000 marks.
"There's a good potential for the market to keep up this recovery," said one Frankfurt trader.

On currency markets, the dollar hit 1.7465 marks in early trade before slipping back slightly to 1.7420 marks after a lower-than-expected National Association of Purchasing Management June dimmed early prospects of interest rate increases.

The dollar's recent rally stems from its safe-haven status amid renewed uncertainty about the strength of the euro after a big split within Germany's ruling coalition over terms of entry for the single currency.

German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Tuesday critics who seek a delay in EMU are making an error and the timetables should be adhered to. "We are sticking to three-point-zero. That is no problem, " he told a conference.

"From the market's point of view...something has got to give, either the timetable or the convergence criteria. Right now, the market believes it is the convergence criteria that will give," Coleman said.

The market will be keeping a close watch on the U.S. central bank's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meeting, which started on Tuesday. No announcement is expected before Wednesday, but economists surveyed in a Reuters poll were unanimous in predicting no rate changes.
In bullion markets, gold closed at $333.65 an ounce. The morning fix was $333.60 an ounce, its lowest since March 30, 1993. Traders saw support if the price fell below $332.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was at 114.80 yen and 1.7420 marks in late European trade, compared with 114.54 and 1.7432 trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index finished up 123.7 points at 4728.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 85.78 points to 2,944.04.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 34.08 points at 3,819.85.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $333.65 an ounce, compared to $334.35 on
Monday. Silver finished at $4.67, unchanged.
